clue.text: Don't agree to amalgamate once more

definitions.meaning: to decline or turn down a request
to join or melt together again

explanation.definitionFit: Declining is the plain sense; the second reading splits the word into the prefix for again plus a verb for melting together.

clue.text: Book is in stock

definitions.meaning: to book a table or seat is to secure it in advance
a stock or store kept back for later use

explanation.surface: A volume is available in the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb meaning to arrange ahead; 'is in' just joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Booking a seat means setting it aside, and a stockpile kept back for later is the noun sense.

clue.text: Produce a brief act in play

indicators.note: something in play is moving about freely, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Stage a short piece of drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like a theatre verb to go with 'act' and 'play', but it means to make up or manufacture.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture or invent something is to make it, as in producing goods or a story.

clue.text: Rates at which the sea comes up on board

indicators.note: on board a ship means within it, so the ship's letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel you would be on board

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word for the sea is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: The speed at which water rises over the deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the convention for putting something inside SS; 'comes up' turns DEEP into PEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Velocities are rates of movement, so the plural noun matches the plural definition.

clue.text: Even so, I'd resolved to take the plunge

indicators.note: resolved here means broken down and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Despite everything, someone has made up their mind to commit to a risky step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' reads as determined, but it signals that EVEN SO I'D is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge steeply downwards, like an aircraft heading for the ground, is the literal sense of the verb.

clue.text: One-time or one time

definitions.meaning: former, as in a one-time champion

explanation.definitionFit: Formerly is the adverb sense; on a single occasion is the counting sense.

clue.text: Match-fit?

parts.note: a sporting term for being ready to play, reread as being suitable for a marriage match

explanation.definitionFit: A suitable bachelor is described as qualified or fit for marriage.

clue.text: Paint turns out to be unsuitable

indicators.note: the letters turn about and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A coat of paint proves to be the wrong choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' reads as 'proves', but it rearranges PAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inappropriate and unfitting are synonyms of the adjective.

clue.text: English queen, one with real potential

indicators.note: something with potential could become something else, so these letters can be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A royal consort who truly showed promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' signals that ONE and REAL are rearranged; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Several queen consorts of England bore this name, among them Eleanor of Aquitaine and Eleanor of Castile.

clue.text: Release a subtle design

indicators.note: a design is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Bring out a delicate pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' reads as set free, but it is RE-LEASE: to lease again to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Renting out a property you yourself rent is leasing it on to another tenant.

clue.text: Busy outside at start

indicators.note: the first word wraps round the outside of the second

parts.note: busy means active, occupied

explanation.surface: Someone is bustling about outdoors from the off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' sounds like outdoors, but here it is a container signal; 'start' is a verb, as in starting an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a machine going is to switch it on or trigger it.

clue.text: Touching sympathy

definitions.meaning: the act of touching with the hands
compassion or tender emotion for another

explanation.definitionFit: Tactile groping is the physical sense; emotional fellow-sympathy is the abstract sense of the noun.

clue.text: Check on expensive-sounding animals

parts.note: to check a horse is to rein it in

indicators.note: sounding means the next word is heard rather than read

parts.note: expensive means dear, which is said like the word for a woodland animal

explanation.surface: Someone checks on costly creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: '-sounding' signals a homophone: DEAR (expensive) heard as DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribou are Arctic deer, the beasts that pull Santa's sleigh.

clue.text: Attend and possibly enlist

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might take another arrangement

explanation.surface: Turn up and maybe sign up for the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attend' looks like 'be present', but here it means pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to a speaker is to pay heed with your ears.

clue.text: Had the best part marked with an asterisk

definitions.meaning: played the lead role in a film or play

explanation.definitionFit: Taking the lead role in a film and being given a little printed star symbol are both senses of this verb.

clue.text: One test out of a thousand

parts.note: ex means former or out, as in an ex-player
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A single trial chosen from a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' reads as a selection, but 'out' gives EX and 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A school examination is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: His work may disturb the sleepers

definitions.text: His work may disturb the sleepers

parts.words: His work may disturb the sleepers
parts.note: sleepers are the wooden or concrete beams under a railway track, which a worker laying the line handles, not people in bed

explanation.definitionFit: A railway worker who lays and maintains track deals with the sleepers that hold the rails.

clue.text: An uplifting sailors' cry

parts.note: uplifting suggests cheering, but the shout is one sailors chant while hauling or heaving up a load together

explanation.definitionFit: The traditional chant of seamen hauling on a rope or capstan together.

clue.text: He wrongly assumes money-lenders carry cash

definitions.note: singular in the clue though the answer is plural; each one wrongly assumes power

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so the lenders wrap round the cash

parts.note: usurers lend money at extortionate interest
P is a penny, a small piece of cash

explanation.surface: A man presumes that lenders have cash about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumes' means seizes, as one assumes a throne; 'carry' puts P inside USURERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who seize a throne or power without right take it wrongfully.

clue.text: Requests put with an attempt at jocularity

parts.note: pleas are requests or appeals
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Appeals made along with an effort to be funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put with' and 'at' are links joining the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light joke or polite banter is a piece of humour.

clue.text: Saw dog's name inside lead

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: Someone saw a dog's name on its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is a noun, an old saying, not the verb; 'lead' is the metal, not a dog's leash.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a traditional saying or maxim.

clue.text: Gosh, it's hard to fit into seat in church

indicators.note: the second piece is made to fit inside the first

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in a church
H stands for hard, as in pencil grades

explanation.surface: Someone finds it difficult to squeeze into a church bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or relief.

clue.text: Is curious about seven world phenomena

definitions.meaning: the Seven ... of the ancient world

explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something is the verb sense; the ancient world's seven great marvels give the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Street name changed — it's a bit flowery

indicators.note: the letters of the word are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A road was renamed, and the result is rather ornate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowery' suggests ornate language, but the definition is literal: part of a flower. 'changed' turns NAME into AMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing organ of a bloom is literally a part of a flower.

clue.text: Smells could be indecorous, not nice

indicators.note: says the letters of the first word could be rearranged, once the letters of the second are taken out

explanation.surface: Bad smells may be improper and unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not nice' tells you to remove N, I, C, E from INDECOROUS; 'could be' rearranges the remaining DOROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scents and whiffs are smells; the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Involved in seeing there's a change of topic

indicators.note: a change means the letters of the next word take a different order

explanation.surface: In watching something, the subject shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a conversation moving on; 'change of' rearranges TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the eye or vision describes the adjective.

clue.text: Hold back and shower after all the others

indicators.note: the shower comes after the others

parts.note: the rest means all the others
rain is a shower

explanation.surface: Restrain yourself and wash once everybody else has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' suggests washing, but it is the weather; 'after all the others' sounds like waiting your turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or keep in check is to hold back.

clue.text: Girl getting rave review

indicators.note: to re-view is to look again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman gets a glowing write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rave review' reads as high praise; 'review' rearranges RAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a girl in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Well held!

parts.note: a cricket shout for a good catch, reread as describing someone held in high regard

explanation.definitionFit: Someone highly regarded is well thought of and respected.

clue.text: Frenchman in our power

definitions.meaning: the French physicist André-Marie of Lyon, pioneer of electrodynamics
the unit of electric current that powers our homes

explanation.surface: A Frenchman holds sway over us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' merely links the two senses: the physicist and the unit named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of current honours the French physicist of that name.

clue.text: Inferior position of some driving instructors

definitions.text: Inferior position of some driving instructors

parts.words: Inferior position of some driving instructors
parts.note: a subordinate role, which is also where a ... driver sits issuing unwanted instructions

explanation.definitionFit: Taking a minor role is idiomatically sitting in the rear of the car, where nagging passengers sit.

clue.text: Vegetables that need to be set in soon

indicators.note: set means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Bulbs that must be planted shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' sounds like planting sets, but it rearranges IN and SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliums grown as bulbs are common kitchen vegetables.
